mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 12-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 12-mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST falls below its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO < -0.5% monthly change.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% in the same month signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5%) alongside a flat or declining unemployment rate (UNRATE monthly change <= 0%) for two months signals labor market imbalances, which historically precede equity corrections and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change <= 0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% and UNRATE monthly change <= 0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An above-trend increase in real personal savings (RSAFS growth > 5% month-on-month) combined with a decline in consumer spending (GDPC1 monthly change < 0%) for two consecutive months signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a pullback in equities over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5% month-on-month AND GDPC1 < 0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS > 5% month-on-month and GDPC1 < 0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for six consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which typically boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months of INDPRO > 0.4% monthly change.
